title: Runtime Stability and Kernel Tuning RC1 — notes and rollout
author: Aisha Banerjee
body:
Summary:

This document captures the RC1 release for the runtime stability and kernel-tuning initiative. RC1 bundles three coordinated changes: (1) the latency-priority preemptive kernel mapper v2 (LP-Mapper v2), (2) conservative batch-splitting heuristics for multi-model pods, and (3) expanded runtime telemetry + profiling helpers. The goal is to reduce p95 generation latency regressions and improve tail behavior on mixed workloads while retaining or slightly improving throughput for steady-state traffic.

Key goals and SLOs:
- p95 single-request generation latency for small sequence workloads (<=256 tokens) <= 120 ms on G4dn/RTX-5000 equivalent GPUs.
- p99 latency reduction target: -15% relative to baseline on mixed burst traces collected 2026-01-12 through 2026-01-18.
- Throughput impact: <= 6% reduction for steady 1000 qps T2-small workloads; aim for neutral impact after automated batching adjustments.
- No increased memory OOM incidents in canary window (see rollout plan).

What changed in RC1 (high level):

1) LP-Mapper v2 (latency-priority preemptive kernel mapper)
- Behavior: incoming low-latency requests get prioritized mapping to lightly loaded shards. If a long-running kernel is running on a GPU, LP-Mapper v2 can preempt queued batches that are not yet bound to a kernel invocation and reassign them to other available devices. Preemption is conservative: kernels already executing are not aborted; only pending batch assignments are moved.
- Configuration knobs introduced: runtime.kernel.lp_mapper.enabled, runtime.kernel.lp_mapper.preemption_window_ms (default 40), runtime.kernel.lp_mapper.util_threshold (default 0.68).
- Expected benefit: reduces p95 by moving short interactive requests off hot shards; may increase cross-device transfer events when preemption occurs — mitigated by the batching heuristics below.

2) Conservative batch-splitting for multi-model pods
- Rationale: observed p99 spikes when large models and small chat assistants shared the same pod under bursty load. RC1 implements a cost model to split large batches only when expected per-token latency savings exceed data transfer overhead.
- New configs: runtime.batch.split_threshold_ms (default 18ms), runtime.batch.cost_per_token (default 0.002 ms/token).
- Example: a 1024-token batch for gpt-small will not be split if predicted split overhead > 18ms.

3) Expanded telemetry and profiling helpers
- New metrics emitted (timeseries names): runtime.latency.generation.p50/p95/p99, runtime.kvcache.hit_rate_p95, runtime.kernel.invocation_latency_ms.p95, runtime.kernel.queue_length, runtime.kernel.preempt_events.count, runtime.batch.split_events.count.
- New high-cardinality trace attributes (added to traces): model.variant_id, shard_id, kernel_version, lp_mapper_decision. Use these attributes in traces only for high-priority samples; defaults are sampled at 0.25%.
- Added a small CLI tool (rwd-rt-profile) to capture a 120s focused profile and upload to internal profiling store. Usage: rwd-rt-profile --target <pod> --duration 120 --label rc1-tuning. The tool ships in /opt/redwood/bin for canary agents.

Performance regression tests and results (canary summary):
- Canary window: 2026-02-15 to 2026-02-21 across us-west1 and eu-central1 test clusters.
- Workloads: interactive chat (median length 48 tokens), long-context summarization (median 1024 tokens), embedding bulk (batch size 128).
- Observed: interactive chat p95 improved by 18% (us-west1) and 13% (eu-central1); p99 improved by 12% average. Long-context throughput decreased 4% on average; embedding throughput unaffected. Memory utilization for multi-model pods increased by 1.8% median (within safe headroom).
- Canary incidents: two minor issues (see Known issues) triggered abort in 1 canary cluster; mitigations applied and rollout resumed.

Profiling playbook snippets (how to reproduce and inspect):
1) Capture focused profile with rwd-rt-profile
- Step 1: identify candidate pod (kubectl -n redwood get pods -l app=runtime,model=gpt-small)
- Step 2: run: /opt/redwood/bin/rwd-rt-profile --target pod/<pod-name> --duration 120 --label rc1-tuning
- Step 3: retrieve profile from profiling store UI or CLI: rwd-profile fetch --label rc1-tuning --since 2026-02-20

2) Quick kernel heatmap (local)
- Command: curl -sS http://localhost:7000/metrics | grep kernel.invocation | sort -nrk2 | head -n 40
- Interpretation: rows indicate kernels by id and invocation counts; high invocation / high latency kernels are the first candidates for specialized kernels or fused ops.

Rollout and rollback plan (operations playbook):
- Canary: deploy RC1 to 5% of serving fleet (us-west1/eu-central1 only) for 72 hours, with an accelerated sampling for latency SLOs (1s sampling window).
- Escalation thresholds (automated):
  - if p95 increases > 10% over baseline for > 10 consecutive minutes -> auto-pause rollout and open runbook incident.
  - if p99 increases > 20% or any OOM error count > 5 in 5 minutes -> immediate rollback to previous kernel mapper (artifact: rp/runtime-kmapper-v1@sha256:ab12ef...)
- Rollout steps (ops):
  1) Tag release: rwd-release tag rc1-kernel-tuning-2026-02-28
  2) Update config: kubectl apply -f patch-lp-mapper.yaml (example below)
  3) Monitor for 60 minutes with telemetry dashboards: Runtime / Kernel Tuning RC1 (dashboard id: rtd-rt-kernel-rc1)
  4) If stable, expand to 25% after 24 hours, then 60% after 72 hours, then full.
- Rollback steps: run rwd-deploy rollback --service runtime --tag previous --region <region> or apply kubectl set image to previous runtime image. Notify SRE channel #sre-runtime and tag incident with "rc1-rollback".

Known issues and mitigations (summary):
- Issue A: Preemption thrash on 8x A100 pods when many small jobs hit concurrently. Symptom: increased kernel.preempt_events.count and small rise in cross-device transfers; in canary this caused two short p99 spikes.
  - Mitigation: lower runtime.kernel.lp_mapper.preemption_window_ms to 20ms for 8x A100 pool (config override), and increase sampling of preemption traces to 2% for diagnostics.
- Issue B: Edge-case OOM on multi-model pods with pinned KV cache when batch-splitting engaged. Symptom: pod eviction with OOMKilled and memory footprint spike after split operation.
  - Mitigation: temporary: runtime.batch.split_threshold_ms -> 30ms (makes splits rarer). Long-term: add soft-limit on kvcache pinned bytes per-model in next patch.
- Issue C: Observability tag cardinality increase caused minor metrics ingestion churn in eu-central; fixed by sampling and batched emission.

Runbook excerpt (immediate responder steps if p95 jumps):
1) Confirm alert: open runtime kernel-tuning RC1 dashboard; check runtime.latency.generation.p95 by region.
2) Check pod-level preempt events: kubectl -n redwood logs <pod> | grep preempt_event
3) If preempt_events.count spike correlates with p95, temporarily set runtime.kernel.lp_mapper.enabled=false for the region:
   kubectl -n redwood patch configmap runtime-config --type merge -p '{"data":{"runtime.kernel.lp_mapper.enabled":"false"}}'
4) If OOMs present, scale impacted nodepool with: gcloud container clusters resize <cluster> --node-pool <pool> --num-nodes +2 (or equivalent). Mark runbook incident and notify ownership.
5) Collect and upload profile: /opt/redwood/bin/rwd-rt-profile --target pod/<pod> --duration 120 --label incident-<id> then attach to incident.

Ownership, contacts, and followups:
- Code owner: eng-serving-runtime/kernel-team (primary: Marco Chen).
- SRE on-call for rollout windows: see oncall rota (link: /confluence/eng-sre/oncall-rotations).
- Followups planned:
  - v1.1: add soft kvcache per-model accounting and eviction policies (owner: runtime-memory-team).
  - v1.2: fuse common attention kernels for gpt-small/gpt-medium to reduce invocation latency (owner: kernel-ops).

Appendix A — example config patch (patch-lp-mapper.yaml):
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: runtime-config
  namespace: redwood
data:
  runtime.kernel.lp_mapper.enabled: "true"
  runtime.kernel.lp_mapper.preemption_window_ms: "40"
  runtime.kernel.lp_mapper.util_threshold: "0.68"
  runtime.batch.split_threshold_ms: "18"
---

Appendix B — example quick diagnostics commands:
- pod heatmap (top 20 kernels): curl -sS http://<pod-ip>:7000/metrics | grep kernel.invocation | sort -nrk2 | head -n 20
- check queue lengths across shards: rwd-rt-cli shard-stats --start -10m --end now --metric kernel.queue_length
- fetch recent preemption traces (sampled): rwd-trace query --tag lp_mapper_decision=true --since 2026-02-14

Notes and writing conventions: this page is intended as the canonical RC1 release note, rollout playbook, and immediate troubleshooting guide. For design rationale, see the kernel mapper ADR page in related_pages. For profiling playbook canonical guidance, prefer the "runtime-profiling-playbook-guidelines-2025" page for full methodology.
